correctness.rationale: The exact method equations specialize to K1_ij=f(d_i) and K2_ij=f(d_i)+(d_i-d_j)g(d_i). The exact Q(1) is the Gram matrix of e^{-at}, e^{-bt}; it is positive definite for a≠b. The METD1 symmetric determinant equals -(f(a)-f(b))²/4<0. Dividing the METD2 symmetric part by a and letting a→∞ yields [[0,-g(b)/2],[-g(b)/2,0]], so eigenvalue continuity gives the exact sharp negative slope. Positivity of g(b) follows from its integral. For a=10,b=1 a rational envelope proves negative determinant; 55 standard-library assertions check formulas and examples without standing in for the proof.

value.rationale: The quantified linear divergence of a negative eigenvalue with stiffness while the physical covariance is bounded and strictly positive is a consequential structure-preservation failure, not merely an observation of nonsymmetry. It shows post-step symmetrization cannot make the published second-order METD covariance step safe and motivates congruence/positive quadrature design. The exact rate is useful for detecting stiffness sensitivity.
